messages.subject: Problems with making a dataframe
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to see if there are any shape and size variation in skulls for male and female polar bears using geometric morphometric. However I have some problems with the testing part. 

I have obtained 30 landmarks using a microscribe, and have used the readland.tps to load my data: 

     readland.tps("pb_skull.tps", specID =c("ID"))
     mydata <- readland.tps("pb_skull.tps", specID ="ID")

To tell whether the skull is a male or female, I have uploaded a classifier document, where I have the ID in one column and the sex in another column:

     classifier <- read.csv("CnSex.csv", header=T, row.names=1, sep=';')

I have performed a GPA and PCA on my data:

     gpa <- gpagen(mydata, curves = NULL, surfaces = TRUE, PrinAxes = TRUE, ProcD = TRUE, Proj = TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)

     pca_skull <- plotTangentSpace(gpa$coords, axis1 = 1, axis2 = 2, warpgrids = TRUE, mesh = NULL, label =NULL , groups =NULL, verbose = TRUE)

I have used the match function to match the pc scores with my classifiers. 

Next I want to test whether they are statistically different or not. For this I have tried to make a data frame, however I think my problems may start here. 
I use my GPA data, and want females and males, and have tried different things: 

     gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(gpa, females = classifier$Sex, males = classifier$Sex)
or
    gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(gpa, sex = classifier$Sex)

However, none of it seems to work. I do not get a dataframe where there are x number of females and x number of males, I get a dataframe where all my specimens are females and the same specimens are also noted as males. I do not know what I should change in my dataframe, so I can use the procD.lm function to test for differences.

I hope you can help me. Thank you. 

Julie Lorenzen

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Problems with making a dataframe
parts:
Julia,

 

When assigning the factor ‘sex’ in the geomorph.data.frame, your second approach is correct: not the first. You only assign it as a factor once, which then has values for each specimen in the dataset: M/F.

 

I have just used some local data in the form of a TPS and a CSV and confirmed that all worked fine. Thus, I suspect that the issue is with your CSV file, or how you are reading it into R.  I suggest you investigate these matters to sort out the problem.


Good luck!

Dean
